    • getOwningType

      public io.micronaut.inject.ast.ClassElement getOwningType()
      The class this method was reached through.

      This used to answer declaringType for a default method, which is every concrete trait method, so withNewOwningType was a no-op for exactly the case it exists for. Class-level AOP advice reaches a method through the owning type's metadata, so a method inherited from a trait and not overridden was never advised: the bean was proxied, the proxy declared the method, and the interceptor chain for it was empty -- @Transactional or @Cacheable on such a method did nothing, silently.

      Specified by:
      getOwningType in interface io.micronaut.inject.ast.MemberElement

    • hasNullMarked

      protected boolean hasNullMarked()
      Whether an absent nullability annotation on this member means non-null.

      `@NullMarked` annotates nothing itself: it changes what saying nothing means for everything inside it. Core leaves that to the language module -- `isNonNull()` on the shared `AnnotatedElement` only asks whether the stereotype is present -- and the Java module implements it by walking from the member out to its owning type. Without the same walk here, every unannotated member of a `@NullMarked` Scala class reported neither nullable nor non-null, so binding and validation treated it as unconstrained.

      Returns:
      true when this member, or the type declaring it, is null-marked
